first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it, read the first screen and sent me two lines: 'A round-up of 12 couples, mostly small weddings. Nothing on scale, exclusive use or privacy.' That is a fair summary. It is calm and not pushy, which I appreciate, but nothing on the first screen tells me this team has done a wedding like ours. I only skimmed the venue questions because she flagged one line.

journey.quote: Every Australia real wedding on this page comes from a story on our own pages: 12 couples, grouped by the setting they chose, whether that was a clifftop, a vineyard, a city room, a garden or an island.
journey.reaction: Clear and honest, but it reads like a magazine index. Nothing here says scale or discretion, so my assistant stops treating it as a shortlist source.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor can plan a wedding anywhere in Australia or abroad and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: We are in Dubai, Sydney and London. The currency line is not what I need to hear. I want to know whether they have run a three-day event for 300 people with VIPs in the room.

journey.section: Real weddings in country and vineyard settings
journey.quote: In New South Wales, [Stephanie and Daniil](/real-wedding-ballet-couple-tie-the-knot-at-australias-wandin-valley) planned a small and playful wedding looking out across the vines.
journey.reaction: Lovely for them. Every card is like this, small and personal. None of them is anywhere near my guest list.

journey.section: Real weddings by the coast and beach
journey.quote: In Wollongong, [Jennifer and Emrah](/stunning-traditional-turkish-and-english-wedding) exchanged vows on a clifftop beside the beach before moving on to a glamorous reception.
journey.reaction: The only card that hints at two families and two traditions coming together, but the text talks about colours and says nothing about how the customs were handled. That is the part I would want to read.

journey.quote: Several of these weddings were small by design, and a smaller guest list asks different things of a space.
journey.reaction: This confirms the page was written for someone else. The planning section is built around small groups.

journey.quote: Is the venue ours alone for the day, or will other events or guests be nearby?
journey.reaction: This is the one question that sounded like us. It is hidden under a small-wedding heading, though, and 'for the day' is not enough. We would need the property closed for the whole stay.

journey.section: Guests travelling from interstate and overseas
journey.quote: Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?
journey.reaction: Sensible, but it is practical, not private. Nothing about private transfers, arrival control or keeping guests away from the public.

journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before heading outside, and again every two hours or after a swim or heavy sweating.
journey.reaction: Too much explaining. I don't need sunscreen tips from my planner. My assistant would skip this.

journey.section: Plan your Australian wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Understated and adult. One contact and terms agreed in writing is what my family office would ask for. It's the best line on the page for me.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Concierge planned weddings of 200 to 400 guests, or events over several days? The page doesn't say.
Can they arrange exclusive use of a whole property for a multi-day stay?
How do they handle privacy: NDAs with suppliers, no social media posts, controlling the photos?
Can they work alongside our own security team and the venue's?
Do they arrange private transfers and VIP arrivals?
Have they handled two cultural traditions, or catering for different faiths and family customs, at this scale?
Is there a private or referral-only way to make contact, rather than a general enquiry form?

turn_offs_found.quote: Trees and built shade cut UV, yet some still reaches guests by reflection, so treat shade as one layer alongside covering clothing, hats, sunglasses and SPF 50 or SPF50+ sunscreen.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. It reads like a public health leaflet, not a planner who would handle all this for me without being asked.

turn_offs_found.quote: Several of these weddings were small by design, and a smaller guest list asks different things of a space.
turn_offs_found.why: Built around small weddings. It makes me feel like a standard client reading the wrong brochure.

cta_reaction.quote: Share with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=australia-real-wedding&utm_content=closing) the setting you picture, the month you are weighing, your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is fine, with no discount or package talk. But I only enquire through a referral or a private channel, and nothing here shows they have handled my scale or that what I share stays private. My assistant might note the name for later and nothing more.

top_3_changes: In 'Keeping the guest list close', ask about exclusive use for the whole stay, not just the day. Old: "- Is the venue ours alone for the day, or will other events or guests be nearby?" New: "- Is the venue ours alone for the day, or for the whole stay, or will other events or guests be nearby?"

In 'Guests travelling from interstate and overseas', add one privacy and security question. Old: "- Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?" New: "- Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car, and can arrivals be kept away from the public?
- Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and who controls access on the day?"

In the closing CTA, invite privacy needs so a discreet client feels expected. Old: "your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel." New: "your guest numbers, how far everyone will travel and any privacy or security needs."

suggested_edits.old: - Is the venue ours alone for the day, or will other events or guests be nearby?
suggested_edits.new: - Is the venue ours alone for the day, or for the whole stay, or will other events or guests be nearby?
suggested_edits.why: Exclusive use across several days is the first thing a large or private wedding asks about. This adds a question, not a fact.

suggested_edits.old: - Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?
suggested_edits.new:
- Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car, and can arrivals be kept away from the public?
- Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and who controls access on the day?
suggested_edits.why: Security and privacy are trust signals for me. Phrased as questions for the venue, so the brand claims nothing new.

suggested_edits.old: your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel.
suggested_edits.new: your guest numbers, how far everyone will travel and any privacy or security needs.
suggested_edits.why: Shows that discretion is a normal part of the brief without making any claim about past work.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant-first skim, private channels only)
No invented brand facts; unknowns listed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings with no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new facts about the real weddings
No more than 3 suggested edits; Australian English; no em dashes
Scores are 1 to 5 on all five required dimensions

assumptions: Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so reactions reflect the card, not real client data.
Reading path follows the card: the assistant skims the first screen and summarises, and Layla reads only the flagged lines.

open_questions.question: This post is aimed at intimate weddings. Is the UHNW persona part of its target audience, or should her low relevance score carry less weight for this piece?
Can the brand say anything verified about large-scale, exclusive-use or privacy-led delivery? If not, the edits above stay as venue questions only.
